IPsec Sentinel – AI-Driven IPsec VPN Protocol Analyzer & Security Assessment Framework

Proposed Solution
AI-driven platform that inspects captured/live IPsec traffic, auto-identifies the exact protocol configuration, and outputs an automated, explainable security assessment.
Addresses the gap between raw packet captures and actionable security judgement — no manual, expert-only Wireshark analysis required.
Novelty: classifies encrypted ESP traffic type via ML flow-fingerprinting (size/timing/direction patterns) and converts findings into a graded Risk Score + Threat Matrix.

Tech stack: Python, Scapy/PyShark (parsing), scikit-learn / XGBoost (ML classifier), Flask/FastAPI + React (interactive dashboard)
Testbed: StrongSwan/Libreswan on Linux VMs (Docker/GNS3) — Tunnel & Transport mode, AES-128/256, AES-GCM, AES-CBC+HMAC, multiple DH groups, PFS on/off, IPv4 & IPv6
Capture: Wireshark / tcpdump for IKE negotiation, ESP, AH and control traffic, labelled by configuration and traffic type (VoIP, web, e-mail, video, ICMP)

Feasible with an open-source stack (StrongSwan, Scapy, scikit-learn) — low cost, modular design, buildable in incremental phases
Core risk: ESP payload is encrypted, so traffic-type inference relies on statistical fingerprinting rather than content — mitigated by a large, well-labelled testbed

Statistical flow fingerprinting (packet size, timing,
direction) instead of content inspection

Broad synthetic testbed covering modes, ciphers, DH
groups, PFS and IPv4/IPv6 combinations

Confidence thresholds + rule-based cross-checks;
human-in-the-loop review for low-confidence cases

Target users: SOC analysts, government / defense network security teams, cloud & enterprise infra teams, security auditors
